BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.

- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.
exchanges.text:
## Overall assessment

The Seller’s update is **not an agreed package**. It materially departs from our playbook on liability, disclosure, completion protections and unresolved diligence. In particular, **neither the 20% cap nor the 18-month claims period is authorised**: each requires prior written approval from Amelia Frost, and none has been given.

The Disclosure Letter also exposes gaps that the Seller’s summary understates. It expressly records missing Bluefen consent evidence, unrepaid Riverlark debt, unresolved Ironquay payment/title evidence and bonuses omitted from the funds flow. Disclosure of these matters does not itself resolve them or satisfy a Completion condition.

## 1. Liability and claims protections

| Issue | Departure and reasoning | Buyer pushback |
|---|---|---|
| **General Warranty cap — cl 12.1** | AUD 4.8m / 20% is only a conditional fallback, not our current position. | Restore **AUD 6m / 25%**. Any proposed fallback requires Amelia’s prior written authority identifying the draft. |
| **Thresholds — cl 12.2** | AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 deductible basket would exclude smaller claims and leave Buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000 even once the basket is exceeded. | Require **AUD 5,000 de minimis**, **AUD 50,000 aggregate basket**, with recovery **from the first dollar once exceeded**. |
| **General claims period — cls 12.3 / 13** | Eighteen months is an unapproved fallback and reduces the period to discover latent problems. | Restore **24 months after Completion**. |
| **Fundamental / Title** | Applying general caps, deadlines and thresholds would materially dilute protection for ownership and capacity—the foundations of the acquisition. “Administrative simplicity” is not sufficient justification. | Separate regime: **100% cap**, **at least six years**, outside the general basket, de minimis and buyer-knowledge bar. |
| **All-Claims override** | The proposal that limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded could pull Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims into the general warranty regime. | Delete the blanket approach and expressly identify which provisions apply to each category. Preserve separate regimes throughout the SPA, not merely in headings. |
| **Fraud and related misconduct — cls 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5** | Applying limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to “all Claims of any nature” conflicts with a non-waivable playbook requirement. | Expressly carve out **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. |
| **Tax / IP purportedly settled** | Seller’s assertion does not establish agreement. These terms remain open; neither general-regime treatment nor unlimited liability should be assumed. | Mark **Tax and IP OPEN**, negotiate their scope and limitations separately, and remove any deemed settlement or hidden general-regime override. |

**Drafting priority:** the carve-outs and separate regimes must prevail across every relevant provision. A standalone Title protection is ineffective if another clause quietly subjects “all Claims” to the general limitations.

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge exclusions

### General disclosure — Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter §§1.1–1.2

The Seller seeks blanket disclosure of the data room, material merely “referred to” there, accounts, registers and public records. This shifts the risk of finding and understanding problems to Buyer.

**Push back:** require **specific fair disclosure**, identifying the relevant matter and giving sufficient detail to understand its nature and scope. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

The specific disclosures should be assessed individually. Their inclusion must not be treated as agreement that they adequately qualify warranties, discharge covenants or cure Completion requirements. The 22 September snapshot also needs updating through Completion.

### Buyer knowledge — cl 8.3

The proposed exclusion extends beyond actual awareness to advisers’ knowledge and anything discoverable from records. Combined with blanket disclosure, it could neutralise substantial warranty protection.

**Push back:** delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion and constructive-knowledge language. Any negotiated **seller-knowledge** qualifier must identify named individuals and require reasonable enquiry. Knowledge must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

## 3. Completion conditions and funds flow

### Bluefen — material customer consent

Bluefen represents approximately **AUD 3.6m / 30% of FY26 revenue**. The Disclosure Letter confirms that neither final written consent nor evidence satisfying its conditions has been provided.

Reasonable endeavours is not an adequate substitute for achieving this material customer consent. Delivery of a consent document alone may leave its conditions outstanding.

**Require before Completion:**
- Effective written change-of-control consent.
- Evidence that all associated conditions have been satisfied.
- Review of the consent and conditions against the underlying contract.

Reject “satisfied on delivery” wording and the suggestion that Bluefen is already addressed.

### Riverlark — debt repayment and security releases

The approximately **AUD 3.2m** balance is not a current payout figure. The facility remains unpaid and no final discharge is included. Completing on a promise of a later release leaves financing and security risk with Buyer.

**Require:** a current payout statement, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective releases of relevant security, coordinated with the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics without double counting.

A post-Completion release requires an **irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia’s approval**; neither should be presumed. Also address the facility’s change-of-control requirements.

### Employee bonuses — omitted Completion cost

The AUD 420,000 bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment. Calling them “a matter for Seller” does not prevent the acquired company from bearing the liability.

**Require:** a specific funds-flow line item or demonstrable Seller funding for **AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs**. Confirm which employment conditions are met and whether superannuation, payroll tax or other on-costs apply. The funds flow must not silently omit them or count them twice.

## 4. Specific diligence risks

### Ironquay IP

The SOW3 payment-only indemnity is too narrow if the real exposure includes defective ownership or transfer of Project Materials and associated third-party claims.

**Push back:** broaden the indemnity to address the identified IP/title exposure and resulting loss, while preserving the **SOW3 payment-and-transfer cure**. Obtain reliable payment evidence and appropriate confirmatory assignment/title documentation.

DD-010’s AUD 180,000 open balance is **not independently verified proof of either payment or non-payment**. Do not treat it as a settled debt, loss or automatic deduction.

### Export/privacy incident — DD-006

The Seller’s “not expected to be material” conclusion is premature. Equally, the record does **not** establish a confirmed breach, unauthorised access, harm, notification duty or monetary loss.

**Require:** preservation of logs and other evidence, a documented investigation into access and scope, assessment of applicable obligations, and continuing updates through Completion. Revisit contractual protection as facts develop; do not invent a numeric demand or assume a notification outcome.

### Sandbar renewals — AUD 330,000

Neither Seller’s “ordinary-course operating costs” label nor automatic Debt classification is supported by the available disclosure.

**Require:** read DD-008 and DD-011 together and establish timing, scope, accrual, cancellation rights, whether commitments are unavoidable, and the services received. Then assess treatment under the agreed price definitions. **No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.**

### Title evidence — DD-012

The supplied share register records Seller as holder of all issued shares, but it is an internal source—not independent verification of ownership, absence of encumbrances or authority to transfer.

**Require:** independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence, reconciled with the register and transfer documents. Retain the separate Title liability regime regardless of diligence.

### Lease and Mossvale — avoid overstating requirements

- **Office lease:** the material identifies a notification obligation, not landlord consent to the share sale. Confirm and satisfy the actual notification requirement.
- **Mossvale:** an assignment restriction does not itself establish a consent requirement for a share sale. Check the complete contract for any separate change-of-control provision.

Do not manufacture consent conditions unsupported by the documents.

## Recommended negotiation summary

1. **Reject the purportedly settled package:** restore the 25% cap, 24-month period and AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 first-dollar thresholds.
2. **Protect separate claim categories:** Title at 100% for at least six years; Tax/IP remain open; no blanket general-regime override.
3. **Insist on mandatory misconduct carve-outs** throughout the SPA.
4. **Reject blanket disclosure and buyer-knowledge exclusions.**
5. **Make Completion protections substantive:** effective Bluefen consent and satisfied conditions; Riverlark payout and releases; properly funded bonuses and on-costs.
6. **Resolve evidence gaps without assuming conclusions:** broaden Ironquay protection, investigate DD-006, assess Sandbar commitments and independently verify title.

Any proposal to use an approval-dependent fallback must be escalated to Amelia before acceptance. Seller wording describing a position as “agreed”, “addressed” or “settled” is not Buyer authority.
